scoring.description: score = readiness * confidence * (w_nov*novelty/3 + w_app*applicability/3 + w_pay*payoff/5 + w_unlock*tanh(unlock_in/1.5) + w_out*tanh(unlock_out/1.5) + w_pull*pull) - w_eff*log1p(effort_weeks)/log1p(26). unlock_in = sum of incoming idea-edge weights from ready_to_use nodes; unlock_out = sum of outgoing weights; pull = 1.0 for bounty/customer/grant, 0.7 for a standard or certification, 0.4 for community demand, 0 for none. For candidates readiness = 0.6 + 0.4 * mean readiness of builds_on (SED counts 0.8). With --goal, score is multiplied by 0.25 + 0.75*keyword_overlap(goal, node text); with --domain, by 0.25 + 0.75*max domain->domain weight into the target domains. Readiness: ready_to_use 1.0, promising_near_complete 0.85, in_work 0.7, candidate 0.6.
scoring.rationale: Payoff and unlock-in dominate so that cheap work sitting one edge away from a READY node outranks ambitious isolated work; effort is log-damped so a 12-week project is not crushed, just discounted.

scoring_proposals.formula: score = conf * (0.20*N + 0.10*A + 0.15*R + 0.25*U + 0.15*P + 0.15*(1-E)); N=novelty tier/3; A=applicability tier/3; R=mean readiness of builds_on (ready 1, promising 0.6, in_work 0.3, SED 0.8); U=min(1, sum over READY builds_on r of w_domain(domain(r)->domain(c)) / 2); P=external pull (bounty/customer 1, standard/cert 0.7, community 0.4, none 0); E=min(1, effort_weeks/12); conf in [0,1]
scoring_proposals.rationale: Unlock in-degree from READY nodes carries the most weight because the purpose of the graph is to compound ready assets; saturation at two strong unlockers prevents gaming via long builds_on lists. Novelty outweighs applicability because zero-sorry theorems are the repo's differentiator. Readiness and effort are symmetric so a 2-week productionization of a ready result ties with an 8-week N3 exploration. Confidence multiplies so speculative edges are discounted everywhere.
